source_record.native_common_basis: Apply deliberate architectural analysis where irreversibility, coupling or quality-attribute trade-offs make late discovery expensive.
common_cost_and_alternative: Account for structural work, requalification, telemetry, isolation, rehearsal, backup, coexistence, maintenance and delayed beneficial change; do not count the same shared capacity twice.

A frozen stage, infrequent release or no change may be adequate; no universal deployment cadence or additional approver follows.
Binding constraints and explicitly nontradeable harms limit the choice set independently of ordinary service-budget economics.
source_record.evidence_ceiling: Root analytical arguments from complete selected native bodies and seven own finite controls. Two bounded practitioner-source accesses corroborate mechanisms, not universal causal effects. No deployed experiment, new property, whole synthesis completion or independent acceptance.

positive_controls.argument: Named interface and quality assumptions identify what reconciliation must actually compare and which mismatches would invalidate the architectural commitment. The contribution is a specific correspondence criterion.
Constraint and coupling analysis identifies the relevant envelope dimensions, representative configurations and high-cost assumptions that qualification must discriminate before commitment.
Coupling, state ownership and quality-attribute analysis make the interaction and candidate separation/control boundaries visible for hazard analysis before an expensive commitment.
Architecture analysis supplies the ordering, compatibility and dependency assumptions that a realistic transition rehearsal must exercise, including commitments that become expensive to unwind.
Architecture analysis identifies shared failure domains and state transitions that determine whether a fallback or recovery path is feasible and which alternatives deserve testing.
Deliberate analysis of coupling and hard commitments exposes maintenance and replacement constraints before they are locked in, contributing to a feasible support concept.
Actual coupling, physical tooling and migration commitments provide named causal cost mechanisms, allowing the analysis to distinguish expensive instances from the rejected unrestricted time curve.
